by_subgroup.AN-Binge/Purging Subtype (AN-BP): Anorexia nervosa binge-eating or purging type

disease_details.evidence_quote: Anorexia nervosa (AN) is an eating disorder with a high mortality.
disease_details.notes: Paper includes both human participants with AN and healthy controls, as well as mouse FMT recipients.

smoker.evidence_quote: smoking history was included as a covariate in analyses and adjusted for
smoker.notes: Smoking status was used as a confounder variable in analyses but not explicitly reported for participants. The inclusion suggests smoking data was collected.

by_subgroup.Anorexia Nervosa (AN): Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, Antipsychotics, Benzodiazepines

treatment.evidence_quote: Exclusion criteria for healthy controls: regular medication apart from birth control pills, antibiotics within 3 months.
treatment.notes: AN patients were treated in specialized centers. Multiple medications were deconfounded in analyses including SSRIs, antipsychotics, and benzodiazepines (Supplementary Table 2).

fmt_role.evidence_quote: faecal microbiota from three randomly chosen AN-RS cases and three age-matched HC participants to three independent litters of female germ-free mice
fmt_role.section: Results — Gut microbiota induces reduced weight gain
fmt_role.notes: Human AN and HC participants served as FMT donors; GF mice were recipients. AN-BP was not used as donors to achieve uniformity.

fmt_id.notes: Study-specific identifiers for FMT participants were not provided in the paper.

neonatal_preterm_birth.notes: Neonatal information was not collected in this adult AN cohort study.

neonatal_birth_weight.notes: Birth weight data not reported for adult participants.

neonatal_gestational_age.notes: Gestational age not reported for adult AN cohort.

neonatal_delivery_procedure.notes: Birth delivery method not reported for adult participants.

neonatal_feeding_method.notes: Infant feeding history not reported in study.

obgyn_pregnancy.evidence_quote: all women in the present study and since ethnicity may influence gut microbiota, we only included Danish Caucasian women
obgyn_pregnancy.notes: While not explicitly stated, AN requires significant weight loss incompatible with pregnancy. Participants were of reproductive age but no pregnancy cases were enrolled.

obgyn_birth_control.evidence_quote: regular medication of any kind apart from birth control pills, and antibiotics within the last 3 months
obgyn_birth_control.notes: Birth control pills were permitted as a medication in healthy controls only.

obgyn_menopause.notes: Menopausal status not reported. Study included women aged 13-53 years (per EDI-3 design) but specific menopausal status data not provided.

biomarker_name.evidence_quote: lower fasting serum concentrations of glucose and insulin, higher insulin sensitivity as estimated by HOMA-IR and lower serum C-reactive protein
biomarker_name.section: Results — Phenotypes of women with AN and controls
biomarker_name.notes: Multiple biomarkers were measured including metabolic, immunological, and microbiota-related markers.

biomarker_value.evidence_quote: Summarized statistics of clinical characteristics are given in Supplementary Table 1
biomarker_value.section: Results — Phenotypes of women with AN and controls
biomarker_value.notes: Specific biomarker values are referenced in Supplementary Tables 1 and 2 but not fully detailed in main text.

biomarker_unit.notes: Units not specified in main text; details in supplementary tables.

disease_response_orr.notes: ORR not applicable; this is an observational microbiota study, not a treatment response trial.

disease_response_pfs.notes: PFS not applicable; this is not an oncology study.

disease_response_recist.notes: RECIST criteria not applicable; this is not an oncology or solid tumor study.

disease_response_os.notes: Overall survival not measured; this is a cross-sectional observational study without mortality follow-up.

feces_phenotype.evidence_quote: Shotgun metagenomics and metabolomics were performed on faecal and serum samples
feces_phenotype.notes: Multiple stool phenotypes analyzed including taxonomic composition, diversity metrics, and functional modules.

feces_phenotype_value.evidence_quote: At the phylum level, AN microbiota samples were characterized by reduction in Bacteroidota and Actinobacteriota
feces_phenotype_value.section: Results — Gut microbiota composition is altered in AN
feces_phenotype_value.notes: Specific values are reported descriptively in results but not in quantitative tabular format in main text.

ecog_performance_status.notes: ECOG performance status not applicable; this is a microbiota study of eating disorders, not a cancer clinical trial.

tumor_staging_ajcc.notes: Tumor staging not applicable; no oncology data.

tumor_size_residual_measurement.notes: This field is not applicable to this study, which focuses on gut microbiota and metabolomics in anorexia nervosa, not tumor measurements.

extraction_warnings: Paper reports aggregate cohort data (77 AN cases, 70 HC controls) without per-participant identifiers or individual sample IDs. Extracted two rows representing the two study groups; individual subject_id and sample_id values are not reported in the paper.

Age is reported only at study-level as 'age-matched' without specific individual ages. age_group 'Adult' inferred from Methods stating participants aged 13-53 years for EDI-3, but most appear adult based on recruitment from specialized treatment centers.
Ancestry inferred as 'European' and 'Danish Caucasian' from Methods: 'we only included Danish Caucasian women with AN cases'. This is a limitation acknowledged by authors regarding generalizability.

Antibiotics exclusion criterion stated as 'antibiotic or antifungal treatment within the previous 3 months' for AN cases and 'antibiotics within the last 3 months' for controls. Recorded as 'No' for current use based on exclusion criteria.

BMI reported as study-level aggregate statistics (AN cases 'much leaner', specific values in Supplementary Table 1) but individual participant BMI values not extracted as per-sample data were unavailable in main text.
Disease reported as 'Anorexia Nervosa' for Case group; HC group listed as 'Healthy' with BMI 18.5–25 kg/m². No specific disease terms for control group.
The paper is cross-sectional, not longitudinal; days_from_first_collection is null as there is only one collection timepoint per participant.
Batch 1 returned granularity='subgroup_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.

Batch 1 subgroups ['Anorexia Nervosa (AN)', 'Healthy Controls (HC)', 'AN-Restricting Subtype (AN-RS)', 'AN-Binge/Purging Subtype (AN-BP)', 'FMT AN-Transplanted Mice (AN-T)', 'FMT HC-Transplanted Mice (HC-T)'] differ from batch 0 []; kept batch 0.

Schema contains many oncology and cancer-specific fields (RECIST, TNM, AJCC staging, ECOG, tumor size, disease_response_pfs) that are not applicable to this eating disorder/microbiota study. These were all marked not_reported.
Biomarker-specific quantitative values are referenced in Supplementary Tables but not extracted in detail from main text due to their presentation in tabular supplements.
FMT mouse recipients are included as a subgroup but most human-specific clinical fields (pregnancy, birth control, menopause) do not apply to animals.
Study has cross-sectional human design and experimental animal design; granularity is subgroup_level based on AN vs HC participant stratification and FMT treatment arms.
Batch 2 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.
study_name: No formal study name explicitly stated in the paper. Derived from trial registration NCT02217384 and research focus.
dna_extraction_kit: Multiple extraction methods reported—IHMS SOP P7 V2 for human samples and NucleoSpin soil mini kit for mouse samples. Reported value is for mouse experiments.

sequencing_platform: Two different platforms used—Ion Proton (Thermo Fisher) for human shotgun metagenomics and Illumina MiSeq for mouse 16S rRNA sequencing. Value represents the primary human study platform.
host_species: Study is mixed-species (human and mouse); both are reported as values in a list.
